title: Scaling Laws (Kaplan vs. Chinchilla): · over-train
prompt: **Scaling Laws (Kaplan vs. Chinchilla):** According to Chinchilla scaling laws ($D \approx 20 N$), if you have a fixed compute budget $C \approx 6 N D$, how should you scale model parameters $N$ vs. training tokens $D$? Why do modern models (Llama 3 8B trained on 15T tokens) intentionally **over-train** way past the Chinchilla compute-optimal point? (Because Chinchilla only optimizes *training* compute, ignoring *inference* cost over billions of future user requests!).
